note: Condensed from the reader's returned report on 13 October 2026; its numbers and the wording of its key observations are preserved.
report:
I read the eleven images with no other sources. Ten of them, every image except X11, show the impressed version of the same four-sign line. Nine are clay sealings: X01-X04 and X06-X10. X05 is an impression with crisp rectangular edges, and X11 is the incised seal that X05 matches. The nine sealings agree with one another in sign forms, spacing and field layout. X05 and X11 carry the same signs drawn to clearly different proportions and a different field, so they come from a second seal.

How I read and measured. In every sealing the light comes from the upper left. The field is sunk below the lump surface, so the upper rim casts a dark band along the top. Each sign stroke is bright on its upper-left flank and casts a dark shadow on its lower-right flank, which means the strokes are raised: these are impressions. The sealings appear to be at a common photographic scale: the first sign and the brackets are about 140 px tall in each one. Hand measurements are good to roughly 10 px.

The four signs, as read on an impression, from left to right: sign 1, a tall U made of two parallel upright arms joined by a rounded bottom (left arm broader); sign 2, a pair of curved brackets enclosing short vertical strokes in two rows, four above and three below where countable, the lower strokes under the gaps of the upper row, the left bracket often ending in a small outward tail; sign 3, two short strokes hanging from the top line; sign 4, an upright oval enclosing a V (left arm a long curve, right arm a shorter stroke), in some images heart-like.

X01: impression on clay; U clear (left arm faint); brackets clear, strokes not countable; sign 3 partly visible; sign 4 clear with a V. Field mostly lost; a narrow vertical ridge below the oval crossed by a short horizontal bar about 160 px below it. Animal unidentifiable.
X02: impression on clay; U clear; brackets clear, strokes blurred; sign 3 as two bumps; sign 4 partly visible. Two or three slanting ridges, possibly legs. Vertical ridge with crossbar partly visible. Animal unidentifiable.
X03: narrow fragment keeping the right end; right bracket only; sign 3 uncertain; sign 4 outline clear. Vertical ridge clear, crossbar 135-150 px below the oval. Animal unidentifiable.
X04: impression on clay with cord or finger grooves above; all four signs clear (three or four upper and two or three lower strokes); oval about 110 px tall. A quadruped facing right with a rounded back and four slanting legs; the head under the last sign; a long vertical element hangs from it almost to the base line, crossed about 150 px below the oval by a horizontal element starting at the head. Identified as an elephant (vertical = trunk, crossing bar = tusk), low to moderate confidence; a different animal with a separate post in front cannot be excluded.
X05: impression with crisp rectangular edges, same direction as the sealings; sign 1 clear, taller than the brackets and about 40 px below them; brackets clear, strokes long bars about a third of the bracket height, four above and three or four below; sign 3 two short strokes squeezed between the right bracket and the oval; sign 4 an oval with a second inner outline and a small V at its top, shorter than the brackets and set high. Field: a long curved ridge from the top-right corner down-left to a point below the oval, a shorter ridge meeting it, a band of about nine oblique parallel ridges at lower right, lumpy forms at the lower right. Animal unidentifiable; at low confidence a horned animal facing right (horn rising forward to the upper right, an ear at its base, folds at the throat). No vertical element with a crossbar.
X06: impression on clay; U at the broken left edge with wavy arms; brackets clear, four above three, left bracket S-curved; sign 3 two crisp rectangular stubs; sign 4 clear. Three long thin lines descend into the field; a long bowed vertical line with a crossbar about 140 px below the oval. Animal unidentifiable, consistent with X04.
X07: impression on clay; U clear; brackets clear, four short strokes above three, staggered; sign 3 two rounded bumps; sign 4 outline clear. A domed head under the last sign with a long tapering element hanging to the base line, crossed by a bar about 155 px below the oval; a long narrow upright oval to its left (ear or foreleg); Z-shaped legs at lower left. Elephant facing right, low to moderate confidence.
X08: impression on clay; sign 1 lost at a break; right bracket and some strokes; sign 3 faint; sign 4 clear. Vertical ridge with crossbar about 150 px below the oval. Animal unidentifiable.
X09: impression on clay; the upper part of the U above disturbed clay; brackets clear, four above three; sign 3 faint; sign 4 partly visible. Vertical ridge with crossbar about 145 px below the oval. Animal unidentifiable.
X10: impression on clay; sign 1 a single upright stroke curving left at its foot, against a crisp left edge of the impression; brackets clear, four above three; sign 3 one or two bumps; sign 4 clear. Vertical ridge with crossbar about 150 px below the oval. Animal unidentifiable.
X11: the seal itself, incised, the mirror image of X05; read mirrored, it carries the same four signs as X05; a long groove from the top-left corner and a hatched band of about nine grooves at lower left, which mirrored is the field of X05.

Same sequence. All eleven carry the same sequence by sign type: U, bracketed strokes, two short strokes, oval with a V. By detailed form the images fall into two groups: Group A, the nine sealings; Group B, X05 and X11. The bracket sign takes 37-41% of the line (left edge of the U to right edge of the oval) in Group A (X01, X02, X04, X07), about 53% in X05 and 54% in mirrored X11. The gap between the right bracket and the oval is 16-19% of the line in Group A and about 8% in X05. The strokes inside the brackets are short dashes about a fifth of the bracket height in Group A and long bars about a third in Group B; the count of four above three is the same. In Group A the oval holds a single V and is as tall as the brackets with its bottom level with theirs; in Group B it holds an inner outline with a small V, is shorter and set high. The bottom of the U is level with the brackets in Group A and extends about 40 px below them in Group B. In Group A the oval ends 20-30 px from the right edge; in X05 about 70 px of space lies to its right, occupied by the curved field line. Each difference is consistent within its group. Within Group A the bracket sign is 0.45-0.49 of the distance from the left bracket's shadow to the oval's right shadow in every sealing. X06 has a line about 5-8% shorter and wavy U arms, X04 a shorter oval, X09 a U stopping at mid-height, and X10 an impression left edge about 35 px from the left bracket where the others have 105-130 px; the first three are attributed to deformation, depth of impression or wear.

One seal or two. Group B comes from a different seal than Group A, on the proportional differences, which hold in both X05 and X11, and on the field: every Group A sealing that keeps the right end has a near-vertical element under the oval crossed by a bar 135-160 px below it, which neither X05 nor X11 has; they have a long diagonal curve and a hatched band instead. X05 and X11 agree in every visible element, which fits X05 being an impression of the X11 seal. The nine Group A sealings are compatible with a single seal. The left edge of X10 is the one observation not explained, possibly clay folded over the left part of the impression, and should be checked on the object.
